findings.explanation: high confidence.  Witness: Let P_1 = (u_1, u_2) and P_2 = (v_1, v_2) with p_1 adjacent to u_1 and p_2 adjacent to v_2, and cross edges (u_1, v_1) and (u_2, v_2). Choosing i, j maximally selects (u_2, v_2), discarding u_1, so p_1 is disconnected from the resulting bipod G' = {u_2, v_2} in G[V(P_1) ∪ V(P_2) ∪ {p_1, p_2}]. Consequently, p_1 and p_2 cannot be connected via a path through G', failing to separate the face C_f into two cycles C_{t_{k+1}} and C_4 as claimed in [p10-2] and [p10-3]. By symmetry, this also invalidates the claim in [p11-1]. Further, choosing i maximally does not even prevent an edge (u_{i'}, v_{j'}) with i' < i and j' > j, so G' may still contain multiple edges between P_1' and P_2'. (p8-1, p10-2, p11-1). Also, Definition 3.2 requires the base edge to be between the lowest indexed vertices (u_{s_u}, v_{s_v}), which are the roots nearest to p_1, p_2, whereas in [p10-2] the edge (v_1, v_2) is at the leaves/descendants, opposite to the orientation used in Lemma 3.3/Definition 3.2. Together these issues invalidate the iterative step for maintaining Invariants I3.4.1–I3.4.6 in Theorem 3.4/1.2.

evidence.text:
We now apply Claim 3.5 to obtain an edge (v₁, v₂) such that w.l.o.g. v₁ and v₂ have colors 1 and 2, respectively. Further, w.l.o.g. v₁ ∉ Bx₁. By Invariant I3.4.5, v₁ is part of a subtree of BFS-tree T rooted at a vertex p₁ of Bx₁. Thus, there exists a path P₁ of length at least one between v₁ and p₁ in T. Similarly, we have that v₂ is part of a subtree of BFS-tree T rooted at a vertex p₂ of Bx₂, i.e., there is a path P₂ of length at least zero between x₂ and p₂ in T. We introduce a new vertex xₖ₊₁ to H and define Bxₖ₊₁ as the subgraph induced by the vertices of P₁ and P₂ without p₁ and p₂. Since v₁ ≠ p₁, we have that |Bxₖ₊₁| ≥ 1. We first observe that Bxₖ₊₁ is a bipod. To this end, observe that each of the paths P₁ and P₂ contains at most one vertex of BFS-layer Li, i.e. they are a vertical path and Bxₖ₊₁ is a bipod.
If Bxₖ₊₁ is not acyclic, by Lemma 3.3 we can find a subset of Bxₖ₊₁ inducing a acyclic bipod such that p₁ and p₂ are connected via a path through that bipod. Thus, Invariant I3.4.2 holds. In H, we connect xₖ₊₁ to x₁ and x₂ and if there is an edge e₃ = (vₖ₊₁, v₃), where vₖ₊₁ ∈ Bxₖ₊₁ and v₃ ∈ Bx₃, also to x₃. Thus, by Construction Rule CR1 of Definition 1.1, H is still a planar quasi-4-tree and Invariant I3.4.1 holds. Moreover, we also immediately yield Invariant I3.4.6. Finally, consider the new faces in the canonical embedding of H. One of the new faces is triangle tₖ₊₁ = (x₁, x₂, xₖ₊₁). Notice that P₁ ∪ P₂ cuts the region inside Cf into two separate parts. One is bounded by a cycle consisting of a path of vertices inside Bx₁, a path of vertices inside Bx₂ and Bₖ₊₁. We define this cycle to be Ctₖ₊₁ = (x₁, x₂, xₖ₊₁).
